stories.headline: Salkilld, Saint Denis to headline UFC Fight Night in Sydney
stories.summary: West Australian Quillan Salkilld will headline a UFC Fight Night lightweight matchup with Benoît Saint Denis in Sydney in February.
stories.body:
West Australian Quillan Salkilld will return to the Octagon in Sydney, after it was confirmed he'll headline the UFC Fight Night with a lightweight bout against Frenchman Benoît Saint Denis on February 7 (AEDT).

Salkilld, 26, is a former Australian rules footballer who turned to MMA after leaving school at 16, and boasts an impressive 13-1 professional record (6-0 in UFC) with five 'performance of the night' bonuses.

The Broome native has won four consecutive fights with a first-round finish, most recently submitting Mateusz Gamrot in their UFC Fight Night clash in Perth in August. He's widely regarded as Australia's next big combat star.

Meanwhile Saint Denis, 30, is one of the lightweight division's most dangerous finishers, and has a 17-4 professional record.

Peter Kloczko, senior vice president of UFC Australia and New Zealand, said the Fight Night -- to take place at Sydney's Afterpay Arena -- would be an "unforgettable event" featuring one of Australia's brightest young stars.

"UFC Fight Night Sydney is set to be another huge moment for Australian fans, and Quillan Salkilld versus Benoît Saint Denis is a main event that delivers everything we look for in this sport," he said in the official release.

"Quillan has been one of the breakout stars of the UFC's lightweight division, while Benoît is one of the most dangerous and exciting finishers in the sport. Bringing this fight to Sydney will make for an unforgettable night."

Further fights on the card will be released in due course.

stories.headline: Power to burn and a 'trademark' goal: why Ethan Drever has rocketed up draft boards
stories.summary: Growing up an Essendon supporter, Ethan Drever hasn't 'seen anything' like success. But his rise up draft boards could have him in the frame to be his childhood club's first pick, writes Jasper Chellappah.
stories.body:
Ethan Drever had absolutely no choice on his AFL team. As a newborn he was put in an Essendon jumper at the hospital and he's been a Bomber ever since.

It's been a rough 18 years of fandom since, and he's got some thoughts about his dad's decision.

"I'm [born in] 2008, I haven't seen anything!" he tells ESPN with a grin - and a grimace.

"Dad tells me about his success and I'm like, 'You don't have to rub it in like that.'"

The Dons are entering a new era in 2027 under Mark McVeigh and it's being driven through the draft. They snagged Sullivan Robey, Jacob Farrow, and Dyson Sharp in the first round 12 months ago and now own pick 1 in the upcoming draft.

Drever also has a lot of thoughts about those drafted before him.

"They've got some good young boys in there now. Robey, Sharp, they're gonna be so good.

"I like Farrow. He should be kicking in and doing all that, he needs to be in priority positions. That's what he's gonna be doing in the future.

"Just that halfback, I reckon he's gonna be really good... he's a beautiful left foot kick."

After a dour two-win season the Bombers have first call on Drever, with the 188cm on-baller strongly linked at the top of the board.

He's an electric runner with the intent to tackle, chase, and pressure - something that hasn't been a trait of Essendon's list for a long time.

Asked what he thinks when watching his boyhood club each weekend, Drever's response would prick the ears of all Bombers fans.

"It'd be nice to be out there and sort of help the boys out, that's kinda what I'm thinking!"

The Vic Country MVP and Rebels best and fairest produced a remarkable season. His star has risen from a first-round chance to the very top of the open pool.

He may have the most translatable traits to AFL level of any prospect. Drever is an elite power athlete, recording a 2.92 second 20 metre sprint which comes across in the tape. He bursts out of the contest with driving legs and loves to exit forward of the stoppage to inflict maximum damage.

His ultra consistent season has come about without any injury concerns, something all other top prospects this year haven't been able to say.

"It's been good not to have to sit on the sidelines this year at all and I can just keep playing consistent footy," he says.

"I only missed one [game] which was just after champs, I just had a break."

Drever lays claim to a pretty handy trademark. On six separate occasions this season he's collected the ball -- either out of a stoppage or in open play -- and powered away from opponents into the forward half of the ground.

From there his long running gait and elite top speed helps him separate from chasing defenders and break the paint of 50 to drive home sensational goals.

"I have heard it's called the trademark goal now. I don't know where that's really come from, it's just a natural thing I guess. I just like to run and have a ping from outside 50," Drever tells ESPN.

"Definitely one of my traits is just my power, especially this year. Building up over the pre-season and definitely my two-way running.

"It's the long-term goal to move into the midfield and be a bit of a Jordan Dawson with his two-way running. I love Finn Callaghan, how he plays. Those two are really great role models for me.

"I think Hugh McCluggage as well, I've watched him a lot. I had a meeting with him this year, he's that sort of two-way runner as well and he's been really good for me."

Drever played 13 games for the Rebels this year in amongst commitments with the AFL Academy and Vic Country. He collected the ball 28 times to go with a goal a game, but he's not satisfied with just being an offensive weapon.

The Ballarat local is a tenacious presence in contests with the appetite to chase and tackle, racking up 6.5 per outing to frank his status as the best pure midfielder in the open pool.

At the draft combine he showed off a much-improved engine running a 6:27 minute 2km after going 20 seconds slower in the lead-up. It's a time that will put him towards the front of the pack on day one of pre-season.

Drever knows exactly what's required to be a midfielder at the next level, and he's determined to get there as soon as possible.

"My endurance side was a big goal of mine, obviously at the top level you've just got to be able to run all day.

"Honing in on my fundamentals and trying to get them the best I can as well. That's what the most important thing is because it's the little one percenters that make a difference in the AFL.

Drever is now on the precipice of living out his dream of becoming an AFL player, and it could be for his boyhood club as the top choice in the open pool of the draft.

That won't matter to him, so long as he gets his opportunity to shine on the big stage.

"I don't really care [if I go at pick 1]. It's nice to have my name up in consideration alongside those boys but I'll just be happy to be picked up wherever I go."

stories.headline: Lens fans banned from Liverpool match for throwing flares vs. Brugge
stories.summary: Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling Tuesday.
stories.body:
NYON, Switzerland -- Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling on Tuesday.

Lens fans lit dozens of flares and threw some toward rival supporters and the field, forcing the team's Champions League game at Club Brugge last week to be stopped briefly. Lens lost 3-0.

The club already were on probation by UEFA for fans lighting flares and fireworks at a previous Champions League game at Slavia Prague in September.

UEFA said its appeals judges imposed a ban on Lens selling tickets to fans for two Champions League away games.

The sanction will be served when Lens play at Leipzig on Nov. 24 and at Liverpool at Anfield on Jan. 27. A third game ban is deferred for a two-year probationary period.

UEFA said Lens were fined €80,000 ($89,000) for charges of "lighting and throwing of pyrotechnics as well as for acts of damage."

stories.headline: Bafana boss Pitso Mosimane's latest South Africa squad shows favouritism fears were unfounded
stories.summary: Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.
stories.body:
When Pitso Mosimane returned as Bafana Bafana head coach, sceptics feared that his proximity to South African club football would lead to an erosion of the meritocratic culture Hugo Broos had built, but the 62-year-old's second preliminary squad suggests it has only been enhanced.

Mosimane began his tenure with Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying wins over Guinea and Eritrea and a friendly victory over Egypt. Next up is the AFCON qualifying double-header against Kenya on Nov. 13 & 17.

Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.

Chicago Fire's Mbekezeli Mbokazi has returned from injury, while Aden McCarthy, Botiumelo Radiopane, Nqaba Xulu, Luke le Roux, Thalente Mbatha, Nkosikhona Radebe, Devin Titus and Thakasani Mbanjwa have also received call-ups.

For every one of these call-ups, a layman can deduce a clear possible motive. McCarthy is the most obvious among them -- he has consistently featured at centre-back for Sabah in the UEFA Champions League and performed well at the highest level.

Radiopane and Xulu are in hot scoring form domestically for Orlando Pirates and Richards Bay respectively. Titus has earned his place with a strong start to life at MAS Fes in Morocco. Mbatha is back from injury and le Roux on the books of a new club at Cercle Brugge after struggling for game time at Portsmouth.

Radebe adds a right-back option from an in-form AmaZulu side with Mamelodi Sundowns' Khuliso Mudau still on the mend from injury. Mbanjwa is rewarded for a strong start to the season in goal for Golden Arrows.

Yanela Mbuthuma and Shandre Campbell -- both of whom have experienced dips in form and fortune at club level since the last international break -- are notable absentees.

In cutting two players he had given opportunities to after they had been mostly overlooked by Broos, Mosimane suggested he is willing to operate without fear or favour.

When 'Jingles' was on the verge of being appointed, Broos was quoted as telling Het Nieuwsblad: "You know, South Africa still don't have a coach. The candidate is Pitso Mosimane, a successful South African coach.

"But they know that if he comes in, they'll go five years back in time. Club owners and agents calling coaches to influence the squad selection. I threw all of them out. If one called, I would say bluntly: 'I don't talk with agents'."

The concern over agents and owners trying their luck in influencing the Bafana head coach may have been well-founded. Broos was not the first to complain of this within the national team setup.

However, questioning if Mosimane himself was open to influence without proof he was willing to make publicly available was ill-advised. It is impossible to accurately speculate on what conversations have or have not gone on between Mosimane and club owners and agents in the two months since then, but what is clear is that his team selection has been thoroughly meritocratic.

The momentum he has garnered is reminiscent of what Broos achieved in the first six months of his tenure.

At the time, the Belgian's irreverent team selection and approach to squad culture put everybody on their toes and led to an uptick in results. After they had failed to qualify for AFCON 2021 immediately before Broos was appointed, the Belgian fell narrowly short of steering Bafana into qualification playoffs for the 2022 World Cup.

In subsequent years, he kicked on and led Bafana to third place at AFCON 2023 (held belatedly in Ivory Coast in early 2024) and the 2026 World Cup round of 32.

When discussing the most successful Bafana Bafana coaches of all-time, Broos should be placed alongside Clive Barker in the top two. However, even the brightest tacticians eventually settle on patterns in their squad selection, and towards the end of his tenure, the Belgian became more predictable in certain aspects.

There was a fairly settled back five of Ronwen Williams, Aubrey Modiba, Mbokazi, Ime Okon and Mudau, and until he switched up his attacking plan to revive the FIFA World Cup campaign, Broos was likely to start Lyle Foster upfront with Evidence Makgopa the main alternative.

In midfield, Teboho Mokoena was a near certain starter and Sphephelo Sithole the clear preferred option alongside him, although Broos occasionally tinkered with his formation and left room for the likes of Bathusi Aubaas and the late Jayden Adams in the holding role. Nkosinathi Sibisi was considered another option, occasionally stepping out from the back into midfield.

Mosimane's arrival has reopened competition for places in these positions. Brooklyn Poggenpoel is retained in the squad after impressing in midfield over the last international break.

After Mbuthuma's minutes upfront, Radiopane and Xulu have been given a chance to earn theirs. Foster has made a second successive preliminary squad, although he failed to make the final squad last time out while in the process of leaving Burnley on loan to Houston Dynamo and settling in.

Fawaaz Basadien, Olwethu Makhanya, and McCarthy are in consideration in the backline. Mudau is, however, still the likely first-choice at right-back for the time being when he returns to full fitness. Still, Mosimane has done well to identify alternatives.

Mosimane declined to get drawn into a war of words with Broos over anything not directly related to matters on the pitch and instead praised his predecessor's impressive record as Bafana head coach.

In his first stint, Mosimane may not have succeeded in the hotseat. However, early results and his approach to team selection suggest he has justified the decision of the South African Football Association (SAFA) to give him a second chance and trust him to navigate the role without fear or favour to anyone.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Flegler move likely; Cowboys keen to keep Nanai
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Flegler move looking likely
Tom Flegler is looking likely to leave the Dolphins at the end of 2027, with ESPN understanding the prop is leaning towards a move away from the club.

While Flegler is yet to make a firm decision, the Dolphins are now facing the prospect of losing him for the 2028 season and beyond.

His future shapes as a situation to watch as the November 1 contracting window approaches.

Cowboys keen to keep Nanai
North Queensland remain keen to retain Jeremiah Nanai, with ESPN understanding the Cowboys are hopeful the back-rower will extend his stay despite preparing to test his value on the open market from November 1.

Nanai has been with the club since he was a teenager, developing into a Queensland Origin representative, and the Cowboys are hopeful that connection will help keep him in Townsville.

Samrani expected to test open market
Jordan Samrani is expected to test the open market from November 1. ESPN understands he will explore his options for 2028 and beyond.

Following a breakout season with the Parramatta Eels, Samrani is open to assessing opportunities elsewhere when the contracting window opens on Sunday.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: What are the Warriors' options as Kristaps Porzingis remains away from the team?
stories.summary: Can the Warriors find a trade partner? Void Kristaps Porzingis' contract? Here's everything we know about the situation, and what could come next.
stories.body:
ON OPENING NIGHT of his 15th NBA season, Draymond Green -- generously listed at 6-foot-6 -- was slotted as the Golden State Warriors' starting center despite a continued organizational understanding about the accumulated toll it takes on his 36-year-old body.

The Warriors' staff gave Green a physical reprieve two nights later against the Memphis Grizzlies' jumbo frontline. But circumstances, which include Al Horford's inability to play bigger minutes in his 20th season, forced Golden State to start Graham Ike, a two-way undrafted center out of Gonzaga in his second career game.

So that still left Green out there in the deciding fourth quarter moments attempting to box out the 7-4 Zach Edey. After failing to wall him off on a defensive rebound, Green committed a crucial frustration foul while the Warriors blew a 12-point lead and fell to 0-2 for the first time since 2020-21.

"We got what we got," Green said when asked about the eroded state of the Warriors' center position. "So we gotta make it do what it do."

The Warriors feel as if part of the reason for their 37-45 failure a season ago was due to a woe-is-me attitude about the fatiguing schedule and injury misfortune, team sources said, so they have taken a purposeful no-excuse approach this regular season.

That has meant an out-of-sight, out-of-mind strategy when it comes to the ongoing absence of presumed starting center Kristaps Porzingis, who was re-signed this summer despite missing 90 games over the past two seasons with three different teams. Ever since Porzingis called out of work one day prior to training camp, the front office instructed Steve Kerr to strategize and prep his team as if Porzingis was a non-factor.

General manager Mike Dunleavy and lead medical decision maker Rick Celebrini are the only members of the team's staff who've been in communication with Porzingis during his absence. Kerr has bristled at nearly every Porzingis question in recent weeks.

"I don't know," Kerr said when asked for a recent update. "I don't really have anything else to add on this."

The decision to make a $20 million bet on the now-invisible Porzingis this offseason looms large over their 1-3 start and their murky path forward. On opening night, the same day ESPN reported the Warriors were beginning to explore possible trade routes while Porzingis contemplates his basketball future, opposing center Walker Kessler dunked on them 10 times, the most in a game for a Los Angeles Lakers center since Shaquille O'Neal in 2003.

In the aftermath, the always diplomatic Stephen Curry was asked about the unfortunate nature of Porzingis' indefinite absence and the impact it is having on his team.

"Aggggh," Curry said, tapping on the table as his frustration seeped through. "It's a hard one for all reasons."

Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago.

"We always said availability was a big factor for our team with all the guys we have out," Curry said. "It's no secret that the (center) spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out."

Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade.

Here is everything we know as the situation remains in limbo.

How did Porzingis and the Warriors get here?
Porzingis' current salary slot was actually created the summer prior during one of the strangest restricted free agency stand-offs in recent memory. Dunleavy and the Warriors were uneasy about committing long-term to Jonathan Kuminga, but felt he still held more value and upside than the sign-and-trade offers on the table.

So they stood firm in negotiations and eventually compromised with Kuminga on a two-year, $46.8 million deal that included a team option and a requirement that Kuminga waive his implicit no-trade clause. They were hopeful he'd contribute, but made their motives clear enough during negotiations that Kuminga's side felt he was being turned into a human trade exception.

The Warriors flipped his contract to Atlanta for Porzingis' expiring $30.7 million contract in February, maintaining salary flexibility while believing they could manage Porzingis' health well enough to get some production out of him.

It worked decently. Porzingis appeared in 15 of the team's last 20 games and averaged 16.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.1 blocks. That gave the front office and medical staff enough confidence to greenlight a two-year, $40 million extension in late June to a player who expressed a desire to continue his NBA career.

Still, the Warriors built in protections for a move they knew carried major risk by only guaranteeing $3 million of the $20 million in the second season. They also structured the extension so Porzingis could be traded immediately instead of having to wait until Dec. 15.

But Dunleavy and the Warriors held belief that Porzingis would be an available rotation piece for chunks of the schedule, not just a tradable contract. There was pre-camp buzz from the coaching staff about the intriguing nature of a Yaxel Lendeborg, Green, Porzingis frontline.

Porzingis was in the practice facility getting court work the week prior to training camp and attended Jimmy Butler's player-led event in San Diego in late September. But optimism faded as team sources in attendance described Porzingis as indifferent and uninterested in participating in scrimmages and strenuous on-court prep work at the event -- a blaring signal of what was on the horizon.

What are the Warriors' options with Porzingis?
Porzingis called Dunleavy and stepped away from the team on the eve of training camp to deal with what they deemed a private health matter. The Warriors gave him some initial space, but expected him to return to the facility and be around his teammates and the medical staff, team sources said.

After a meeting with Celebrini and Dunleavy in early October, the team sent out a statement declaring he would be around. It didn't last. Porzingis hasn't returned to the facility and the organization shifted his official status from out with "general illness" (as they'd listed during his absences last season) to "not with team," a purposeful change. This can no longer be described as an excused absence for the center.

Porzingis' unwillingness to be present at the Warriors' facility could be deemed a failure to render his services -- a reality that has been raised internally, sources said -- and could be used in an attempt to void the entirety of his contract. But that would present its own complications, unless Porzingis expressed an intention to retire and willingly gave all the money back.

The Warriors are currently $20.4 million into the luxury tax. Wiping away Porzingis' salary erases nearly all of their tax bill, ducks them under the first apron and gives them more trade flexibility, but it doesn't free up a major roster-building tool in the immediate. They'd only be able to add a player on the minimum via free agency.

The Warriors had a similar situation two seasons ago. They signed De'Anthony Melton to a one-year, $12.8 million deal in July 2024. He tore his ACL in early November and was ruled out for the season.

In response, Dunleavy lined up a trade with the Brooklyn Nets for Dennis Schroder, set to be executed on the first day Schroder was eligible to be traded (Dec. 15). It cost them a net of two second-round picks. Schroder played 24 games with the Warriors before he was traded as part of a deadline deal to acquire Butler.

That'd profile as a preferred route for the Warriors in this current Porzingis jam -- utilizing a minor asset to acquire a usable rotation player in the interim while maintaining the flexibility to repackage that expiring number for a larger swing at the deadline.

But under the new anti-tanking rules, there aren't any obvious trade partners ready to part with a usable player for a minor asset, especially in late October. Dunleavy has already gauged the temperature on the trade market, league sources said, but this is traditionally a quiet time in that respect. Front offices are typically in fact-gathering mode about their roster before making bigger picture decisions closer to January and February.

Right now, the Warriors are showing a willingness to remain patient with the Porzingis contract and let the market materialize, league sources said. If Porzingis proves willing to give back a large chunk of money in a buyout, his expiring $20 million deal could become even more financially appealing for an eventual trade partner attempting to gain some financial benefit.

What is the Warriors' plan in the interim?
Lendeborg's immediate success has brightened the mood and eased some concern around the Warriors. The rookie wing had 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in a surprising blowout win in Denver on Monday night.

Lendeborg's size (at a powerful 6-10 and 241 pounds) has allowed them to downsize with Green at center while feeling bigger than their previous small-ball lineups. Lendeborg has 37 rebounds in four games.

Their current starting lineup (Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Lendeborg, Green) is a plus-22 in a small early season sample. Horford -- limited to around 20 minutes per game and unable to play back-to-backs -- has looked fresh in brief doses.

While evolving through a semi-rebuild, the Warriors have shown an increased willingness to give opportunity to their youth in an effort to unearth some gems and improve their long-term outlook.

Ike has started two of the first four games, but will be limited to 50 games total unless the Warriors can convert his two-way contract to a full deal. Charles Bassey, the 25-year-old journeyman who is attempting to catch on with the Warriors after five previous stops, provides another big body off the bench.

"I love the attitude of this team," Kerr said. "I love the energy, the spirit. I like our talent. Then I think our two young big guys are good players."

stories.headline: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Ranking the top 25 candidates to move, plus team fits
stories.summary: Could the Colts listen on Jonathan Taylor? Would Josh Sweat help a contender's defense? We stacked the top players who might move before the Nov. 10 deadline.
stories.body:
We're less than two weeks away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline (Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET). Which players could potentially be available? And which trade candidates could make the biggest impact with new teams if they do get moved?

NFL analyst Matt Bowen and national NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler worked together to build a comprehensive list of the top 25 possible trade candidates. To be clear: Players are ranked here by the potential value they'd provide a new team if traded -- not their likelihood of actually being dealt.

That said, we did include our estimated percentage chances for each player to move, weaving in what we're hearing. Jeremy shared the latest buzz on each player, while Matt broke down what he sees on the tape. We even included some interesting team fits for each candidate. Some players have better odds of changing cities than others on the list, but all 25 are at the very least being discussed in trade conversations. Let's dive in.

Jump to the top-ranked:

QB | RB | WR | TE | OL

Edge | DT | LB | CB | S

1. Jonathan Taylor, RB, Indianapolis Colts
What Fowler is hearing: Teams I've talked to aren't totally sold that Indianapolis will trade Taylor despite heavy interest -- at least not yet. He is signed long term and would be a boon for next year's coaching staff, whether it's the current group or entirely new. But what Kenneth Walker III has done for Kansas City shows how a premier running back can put on new jersey colors and immediately reimagine a team's season. And the tenor of Indy's season is getting ugly, which affects all key players and could spark even more movement.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 30%

What Bowen sees on tape: Taylor is averaging 109.3 total yards per game this season, and he's tied for first in rushing TDs with eight. He's a volume runner with home run speed and pass-catching ability on screens and swings. His 17 rushes for 10 or more yards are tied for the fourth most in the league. Taylor would be an immediate upgrade for a team in need of a lead back who is decisive with the ball.

Team fits: Seahawks, Commanders, Saints, Broncos, Vikings

2. Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars
What Fowler is hearing: League execs are sensing the end for BTJ in Jacksonville, as his targets and playing time have dipped. How Jacksonville has struggled to make this relationship work is still a mystery. Thomas is an elite mover with size who draws coverage deep, setting the stage for teammates Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers to eat underneath. But that plan for Thomas hasn't materialized this season. And teams are circling with interest. Kansas City and Pittsburgh are among those exploring receiver help.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 45%

What Bowen sees on tape: Thomas' numbers have declined over the past two seasons, but he has the traits to still draw interest. At 6-foot-3 and 209 pounds, Thomas has the profile of an X receiver who can separate at multiple levels of the field. I see legit straight-line speed and ball-tracking ability. He had 87 receptions and 10 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024, but he has been limited to a 9-105-1 line so far this season.

Team fits: Chiefs, Steelers, 49ers

3. Josh Sweat, Edge, Arizona Cardinals
What Fowler is hearing: Rival teams could see him getting moved. "Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense to me," an NFC exec said. "That's a profile fit." Rumblings persist that Sweat would want a new contract -- he's in the second year of a four-year, $76 million deal -- and that could complicate things. But many teams are looking for an edge rusher.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 40%

What Bowen sees on tape: A long, angular mover who can win with speed-to-power, Sweat had 12 sacks and 37 pressures in Arizona last season. But his numbers haven't been as solid in 2026, with two sacks and 10 pressures. Still, Sweat's ability to threaten the edges of offensive tackles with his quickness off the ball fits pass-rush fronts across the league.

Team fits: Cowboys, Bears, 49ers

4. Yaya Diaby, Edge, Tampa Bay Buccaneers
What Fowler is hearing: Tampa Bay beat Carolina handedly in Week 7, with Diaby exploding for three sacks. A loss would have put the Bucs at 1-6 and closer to dealing mode. Diaby, 27, is still on the radar, though, because Tampa is not poised to pay the 2027 free agent, and the emergence of second-year rusher David Walker (four sacks) gives the Bucs a natural replacement. Diaby needs a new contract, but an acquiring team could get a compensatory pick for him if he signs a substantial deal with another team in free agency.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

What Bowen sees on tape: Diaby is a powerful and physical edge rusher with the temperament to set the edge against the run. He has three sacks and six tackles for loss in 2026, and he had 40 or more pressures in each of his past two seasons (with 11.5 total sacks over that time). He should be viewed as a quality starter.

Team fits: Browns, Seahawks, Cowboys

5. Jerry Jeudy, WR, Cleveland Browns
What Fowler is hearing: The Browns are not actively sending out feelers on Jeudy, but they would at least consider a substantial offer. Key word here is "substantial," though. I'm not sure, say, a fourth-round pick would move anyone in Cleveland, for example. Jeudy is part of the Browns' three-receiver sets and the veteran in that room for a good team in the playoff hunt. That dynamic diminishes his chances of being dealt. But as always, teams are looking for receiver help.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 20%

What Bowen sees on tape: Jeudy has the route traits and stop-start speed to separate as a multilevel route runner. He's sudden at the break point. However, the inconsistent hands have been an issue as a pro (33 career drops), and Jeudy lacks the frame and physicality to win on 50-50 throws. Jeudy had a career-best 1,229 receiving yards in 2024, yet he has just 16 receptions this season.

Team fits: Chiefs, Raiders, Commanders

6. Daron Payne, DT, Washington Commanders
What Fowler is hearing: Washington dealt key defensive pieces at the deadline three years ago and could be faced with a similar predicament this time with Payne, who's 29 and still has value. Payne is a 2027 free agent with a $16.4 million base this year. But the NFC East is also winnable, despite Washington's 1-4-1 record, so that could be a point in favor of the Commanders keeping him. Jacksonville is a potential fit, with some in the league noting the Jaguars could use a versatile interior player with pass-rush ability and have looked for that since the offseason.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 25%

What Bowen sees on tape: Payne can still provide an interior presence due to his foot quickness and strength in one-on-one matchups, plus he will impact the run game from multiple alignments. He had a career-best 11.5 sacks in 2022, but he has totaled only 12 over his past four seasons.

Team fits: Jaguars, Giants, Buccaneers

7. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers
What Fowler is hearing: Mack is productive and affordable. The Chargers gave him a $10 million signing bonus in March, so a new team would inherit the prorated version of his $8 million salary to close out his one-year deal. Returning to the Bears is a natural fit for the equivalent of a quality Day 3 pick. The Chargers have held off trading pieces such as Mack up to this point, though.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

What Bowen sees on tape: Mack doesn't display the same level of explosive speed on tape, but he can still disrupt the pocket due to his play strength and advanced counter moves. Mack has 14.5 sacks and 83 pressures over his past three seasons, and he can play as both a pass-rushing linebacker or defensive end with third-down upside.

Team fits: Bears, Browns, Bills, Cowboys

8. Riq Woolen, CB, Philadelphia Eagles
What Fowler is hearing: When I talk to rival teams about which players Philly might move, Woolen's name comes up fairly often. He's a high-upside corner and 2027 free agent whose $1.26 million base salary could help facilitate a trade (much of his $12 million in guarantees came via signing or restructured bonuses).

Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

What Bowen sees on tape: Woolen has the length and long speed at 6-foot-4 to help a defense majoring in man coverage and two-deep zone. The tackling and eye discipline could improve, but Woolen is a disruptor on the perimeter. In five pro seasons, he has 12 interceptions and 57 pass breakups.

Team fits: Lions, Panthers, Steelers

9. Budda Baker, S, Arizona Cardinals
What Fowler is hearing: A few wins won't camouflage Arizona's transitional state -- and it needs draft capital to finish the rebuild. Baker, who has seven consecutive Pro Bowls and has 3.5 sacks on the season, could help get the Cardinals some extra picks. Long a favorite in coaching circles, Baker would garner strong interest. He's owed $16.2 million this year and $17.8 million next year. People I've talked to believe the Cardinals should try to get something for Baker.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

What Bowen sees on tape: With his downhill speed and urgency to the ball, Baker remains a disruptive safety who can play in split-field schemes or roam near the line of scrimmage. He isn't a high-level playmaker in coverage (nine career interceptions), but his ability to defend the run and blitz creates an impact in the game plan.

Team fits: Bills, Jaguars

10. Patrick Queen, LB, Pittsburgh Steelers
What Fowler is hearing: Rumors of a Queen trade persisted in the spring, with the Cowboys among teams that checked on his availability. He's also a 2027 free agent. But the Steelers' status as a 5-2 team likely keeps him in Pittsburgh.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 20%

What Bowen sees on tape: Queen is a run-and-hit defender with lateral pursuit speed. He can track the ball on the perimeter and close quickly on underneath throws as a zone defender. Queen struggles at times as a run defender in tight quarters, and his route identification can improve, but he has had at least 115 tackles in each of his four previous seasons. And he has 26 pass breakups over the past five years.

Team fits: Cowboys, Bills

11. Jermaine Johnson II, Edge, Tennessee Titans
What Fowler is hearing: Teams in the market for an edge rusher believe Johnson could be available at the right price. The Titans are reeling at 1-6 and are still in rebuilding mode, which necessitates adding more draft picks. Johnson is a Robert Saleh favorite from their Jets days together and just got to Tennessee via an offseason trade. But enough interest in the edge-rush market could make him a factor. Teams I talked to consider him a toss-up to be traded.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 30%

What Bowen sees on tape: I don't see elite traits with Johnson, but he has the play strength and length to dent the pocket, and he will pick up second-reaction hits on the quarterback due to his effort level. Plus, Johnson will hammer the ball back inside when setting edges as a run defender. Johnson has 16 career sacks over five pro seasons.

Team fits: Browns, Bears

12. Landon Dickerson, G, Philadelphia Eagles
What Fowler is hearing: Something feels off between the Eagles and Dickerson, one of the holdovers from the Jeff Stoutland offensive front. He recently took what appeared to be a passive-aggressive shot at the front office over his long-term outlook with the franchise. The Eagles are in a position to recoup draft capital for the future and are going younger on the offensive line. A mix of erratic play and injuries could affect his value, but he has Pro Bowl traits, his guarantees run dry next year, and he held up well in his return for "Monday Night Football" against the Cowboys.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 25%

What Bowen sees on tape: A Week 1 injury sent Dickerson to injured reserve, but he returned this past Monday. And when healthy, Dickerson can move defenders off the ball as a run blocker in both zone and gap schemes, and he can set an anchor in pass protection to handle power down his middle with his 6-6, 332-pound frame. In five seasons with the Eagles, Dickerson has a pass block win rate of 93.9%.

Team fits: Chargers, Packers

13. Josh Downs, WR, Indianapolis Colts
What Fowler is hearing: The Colts opened the floodgates with the Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner deals, and Downs -- the team's best receiver with Alec Pierce out -- has garnered interest from multiple teams. He's a 2027 free agent and would probably welcome the chance to play with someone like Patrick Mahomes if the Chiefs were to come calling, due to the Colts' sagging passing game.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 45%

What Bowen sees on tape: Downs has the sudden footwork and coverage recognition to uncover between the numbers. In four pro seasons with the Colts, he has 224 receptions and 11 touchdowns. He fits a team looking for a high-percentage target to win underneath and move the chains.

Team fits: Chiefs, Steelers

14. Donte Jackson, CB, Los Angeles Chargers
What Fowler is hearing: Corner is a position of need for several teams, and the Chargers likely could get a draft pick for Jackson. The 30-year-old has ball production and a reasonable contract -- a $6 million base salary. Plus, he is set to hit free agency in March.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 25%

What Bowen sees on tape: With his backfield vision and short-area closing speed, Jackson fits best as a zone corner. He's a top-down defender with route awareness who can create on-the-ball production. Jackson has 23 interceptions and 68 pass breakups over his career.

Team fits: Panthers, Lions, Ravens

15. Shemar Stewart, Edge, Cincinnati Bengals
What Fowler is hearing: While the Bengals typically don't trade away recently drafted players, Stewart is out of the defensive end rotation and would have value. He was inactive Sunday in Baltimore. He has high upside and turns 23 in November. The emergence of rookie Cashius Howell gives Cincinnati cover should it move on, too. Stewart is a name a few teams have had circled as a possibility for weeks, and teams predict a Day 3 pick would be the most likely value.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

What Bowen sees on tape: Stewart has played just eight snaps this season, so teams would be betting on potential with the 2025 first-rounder. Stewart is an explosive mover with the physical profile to play on the edge, but he has yet to develop a refined pass-rush plan. He has two career sacks.

Team fits: Eagles, Lions

16. Jauan Jennings, WR, Minnesota Vikings
What Fowler is hearing: The Vikings' free agent addition is not a focal point of the offense and is considered a trade candidate leaguewide. But he did catch two passes for 34 yards Sunday against the Colts for a Minnesota passing game that's not exactly thriving right now. Jennings, who's on a one-year deal, could prove a low-cost option for teams looking to add to their receiver room. The 49ers are an obvious fit.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 50%

What Bowen sees on tape: Jennings has seen very limited opportunities in Minnesota this season, catching just four of eight targets. However, he has proved to be a reliable target in previous seasons. He's a consistent route runner who plays through contact and makes himself available to the quarterback on in-breaking targets.

Team fits: Rams, Falcons, 49ers

17. Chris Godwin Jr., WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers
What Fowler is hearing: Godwin is a legacy Buc through 10 seasons, but he hasn't been quite the same since his 2024 ankle injury. His veteran presence and savvy play could help another team. He's due $22 million in cash this year, which could be a deterrent to a deal, though.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 15%

What Bowen sees on tape: Godwin has yet to top 50 receiving yards in a game this season, and his play speed is declining. However, he still has value as a slot target with outside flex. He can use his coverage awareness to find open grass. And Godwin is willing to work the heavy traffic areas of the field on middle-of-the-field concepts.

Team fits: Chiefs, Commanders

18. Rashod Bateman, WR, Baltimore Ravens
What Fowler is hearing: This one is a bit of a wild card, as the Ravens aren't overly deep at receiver. But Bateman has long been a bit miscast in Baltimore. He's not a focal point of the offense -- he's more of a secondary option who can clear out to lift safeties -- but he would probably like to be featured more. Teams have had interest in the past, and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is well-positioned for WR2 status in Baltimore.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 15%

What Bowen sees on tape: Bateman fits as a perimeter target with separation speed and ball-tracking ability to win on third-level throws and in-breakers. He can be re-routed, and he isn't a contested-catch specialist, but he fits as a No. 3 target with the ability to play Z or X. Bateman has 16 touchdown receptions in his career.

Team fits: Commanders, Chiefs

19. Jackson Powers-Johnson, G, Las Vegas Raiders
What Fowler is hearing: Johnson-Powers was benched in Week 6 and would probably welcome a change at this point. Several teams are combing the guard market, and Powers-Johnson wouldn't cost as much as the marquee names. A Day 3 pick swap might get something done, allowing the Raiders to improve positioning on the back of the draft order.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

What Bowen sees on tape: Powers-Johnson has the traits to play both center and guard, and he had a 93.3% pass block win rate as a rookie in 2024. However, he was limited to eight games last season due to an ankle injury, and his 2026 tape shows a regression as a run blocker (career-low 62.7% run block win rate). Teams that had a high draft grade on Powers-Johnson could try to make a move here.

Team fits: Jaguars, Chargers

20. Quentin Johnston, WR, Los Angeles Chargers
What Fowler is hearing: Teams have considered Johnston a trade candidate dating back to March. The Chargers shut that down at the time and even exercised his fifth-year option. But the Chargers' 0-6 plight is resurfacing his name in league circles.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 25%

What Bowen sees on tape: With his physical tools at 6-3 and 208 pounds, plus the straight-line speed to create explosives, Johnston can help a team as a No. 3 receiver. The drops have been an issue in his four-year career (11 total), and he has been limited to only eight receptions this season. However, Johnston has 18 career touchdowns, and he produced 700 or more receiving yards in both 2024 and 2025.

Team fits: 49ers, Raiders, Steelers

21. A'Shawn Robinson, DT, Tampa Bay Buccaneers
What Fowler is hearing: Robinson is a name that a few teams floated to me because he's still a productive interior player and a veteran who could help a contending team. He also wouldn't cost much to acquire at this stage. He has played for four other teams -- the Lions, Rams, Panthers and Giants -- so he has coaching friends all over the league.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 30%

What Bowen sees on tape: At 6-3 and 320 pounds, Robinson is a powerful run defender who can play as a 1-technique nose or 3-technique defensive tackle. While Robinson doesn't provide pass-rushing upside (16 career sacks), he can push the interior of the pocket. He's an early-down defender who could help out a defensive line rotation. He even has two interceptions this season!

Team fits: Rams, Ravens, Giants

22. Kirk Cousins, QB, Las Vegas Raiders
What Fowler is hearing: Cousins played well enough through seven games that he has trade value. So does his contract, which after being reworked features a $1.3 million base salary. Aidan O'Connell, the Raiders' QB3, is a former starter who could slide into the primary backup role to Fernando Mendoza if Las Vegas is ready to start the rookie. There are no glaring needs at quarterback leaguewide, but injuries happen every week. The Raiders have not planned to be overly active at the deadline.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 20%

What Bowen sees on tape: What Bowen sees on tape: He's a pocket thrower who wins with timing and ball location. Cousins can read it out post-snap and play as a ball distributor. He lacks the mobility to make plays outside of structure at a consistent rate, but he can get to the edges on boot concepts, and he fits best in a system that incorporates play-action elements. Cousins has thrown 16 touchdown passes and five interceptions this season.

Team fits: Panthers, Giants, Vikings

23. Cesar Ruiz, G, New Orleans Saints
What Fowler is hearing: The Saints could explore trade options while sitting at 2-5, and several teams are looking for a quality guard. New Orleans has to win and already lost a starting offensive lineman in tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., so this is hardly a slam dunk. But he's an intriguing name about whom teams could inquire.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 25%

What Bowen sees on tape: Ruiz is a capable player in pass protection, using his foot quickness and technique to slow interior rushers. He has posted a pass block win rate of 90% or better in five of seven pro seasons. However, Ruiz isn't a natural displacer at the point of attack in the run game, which impacts his ability to create consistent movement. His career run block win rate sits at 66.8%.

Team fits: Lions, Commanders

24. Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans
What Fowler is hearing: Several teams could use a running back, and Pollard is an attractive fallback plan if the Colts stand pat on Taylor. But as one AFC exec pointed out, "I don't think [the Titans] want to take weapons away from the quarterback right now." Indeed, Cam Ward needs his supporting cast in an important second season. His three-touchdown performance Sunday vs. Cleveland shows his value in Tennessee.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 15%

What Bowen sees on tape: Pollard is a slasher. With change-of-direction ability and vision to find daylight, he had his best day of the season in Week 7, producing 155 total yards against the Browns' defense. Pollard's receiving traits have been minimized in a struggling Titans offense this season, but he had 30 or more catches in each of his previous five seasons. He's a dual-threat back who could step into a lead role -- if the Titans decided to make a move.

Team fits: Commanders, Vikings

25. Alontae Taylor, CB, Tennessee Titans
What Fowler is hearing: Taylor is not an easy player to trade because of his contract, which guarantees his entire 2027 salary of $20.5 million. But as one NFC exec put it, Taylor was the best corner in free agency in March, and that type of player has value no matter what.

Predicted chance of getting traded: 10%

What Bowen sees on tape: Taylor has gotten off to a slow start with the Titans after signing in free agency. However, he plays a premium position, and he has the speed to cover receivers on the perimeter or play a disruptive role in the slot. In his four seasons with the Saints before joining Tennessee, Taylor had four interceptions, 40 pass breakups and seven sacks.

stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Mexico on a weekend where Kimi Antonelli could win the drivers' championship for the first time.

The Mercedes driver extended his lead in the title to 123 points from George Russell after winning the United States Grand Prix. He will simply need to finish ninth or higher in Mexico City to seal the title.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was looking strong in the upgraded Ferrari to finish second in Austin, with Max Verstappen on the final step of the podium.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 19th round.

- F1 readies Antonelli's title champagne in Austin: 'The race of a champion who isn't champion yet'

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Mexico City Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
Mexico City is one of the most vibrant atmospheres on the calendar and fans congregate in the thousands to cheer on home hero Sergio Pérez.

It's a true anomaly on the calendar due to the high altitude of of 7,300 feet (2,200 metres) and therefore presents a unique challenge for the teams and drivers. Teams can run Monaco-level downforce packages while still reaching Monza-esque top speeds.

One of the iconic parts of the track -- the Foro Sol stadium section -- includes two tight corners in a former baseball stadium.

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1963

Laps: 71 laps of 4.3km

Lap record: 1:17.774, Valtteri Bottas (2021)

Most wins: Verstappen with five (2017-2018, 2021-2023). Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2016, 2019), Sainz (2024) and Norris (2025).

Most poles: Jim Clark with four (1963-1965, 1967). Other pole sitters from the current grid are Hamilton (2016), Leclerc (2019, 2023), Verstappen (2022), Sainz (2024) and Norris (2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Mexico City Grand Prix is set to reach temperatures of 27°C for qualifying and Sunday's race, with no rain due.

What happened last time out?
Norris pulled out a thrilling lap to take pole position in Mexico, his first pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July. The Brit said on the team radio afterwards "What a lap. What a lap. Even I don't know how I did that."

It was a dominant race weekend from the McLaren driver after he became the new leader in the title race ahead of his teammate Oscar Piastri for the first time since April.

He had a one point advantage over Piastri with just four races to go.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli put his Mercedes on a surprise pole in Austin and converted it into another victory as he inches closer to taking the title crown with five races remaining.

The youngster will need just two points this weekend, or for Russell and Hamilton to not win the race, to get the job done in Mexico.

Red Bull are a looming threat each weekend after bringing major upgrades and Verstappen will be one to watch out for. He's also got five race victories under his belt around Mexico City.

All eyes will be on Antonelli. He will be hoping to wrap up the title and is looking like he's in a position where nobody will be able to stop him.

stories.headline: Dream say concerns over finding available WNBA Finals venue went unheeded
stories.summary: In a letter to the city, the Atlanta Dream said Game 6 getting moved to 12:30 p.m. so they can play in State Farm Arena was "not what we fought for."
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- In an open letter addressed to the city, the Dream said concerns they had over the availability of a properly sized venue for WNBA Finals games in Atlanta went unheeded and that the solution of moving Game 6 up to 12:30 p.m. ET was "not what we fought for."

Game 6 between the Dream and Golden State Valkyries will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. as opposed to the originally scheduled 8 p.m. The shift in timing was a result of the game being moved to State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks.

The Dream have played all their home games this postseason at State Farm Arena, which seats roughly 17,000 fans. Their home court, Gateway Center, fits just 3,500.

To accommodate Game 6, the Hawks' home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers that night will move back one hour to 8 p.m. To accommodate Game 4 at State Farm Arena, the Hawks' home game this past Saturday was moved to 8:30 p.m. All three Finals games in Atlanta have required hurried adjustments to the schedule.

"As much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage," the letter said. "That meant State Farm Arena."

In the letter, the Dream said they brought up concerns involving potential playoff scheduling and dates that overlapped with NBA games at the arena two months ago. The organization said that while it reiterated the issues as the playoffs went on, "our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

Sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou that the dates for the 2026 playoffs were sent internally to teams on Dec. 4, 2025.

Negotiations between the WNBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, NBA and broadcast partners took place over the weekend to figure out the best course of action for all parties involved.

The NBA and WNBA explored options to keep Game 6 in primetime, ESPN's Ramona Shelbourne reported. However, the Hawks and Cavaliers both play Wednesday night, so they could not play their game in the earlier time slot Thursday.

"I hope everyone gets to see it somehow, and I know for some people it's not realistic -- they have jobs and won't be able to make it," Dream coach Karl Smesko said ahead of Game 5 in San Francisco. "I'm disappointed for that, but I'm hopeful as many people as possible can see the game."

In a statement Monday, WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert added: "The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line. We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta."

Valkyries players Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton encouraged fans in the Bay Area to call in sick to watch the game, while their coach, Natalie Nakase, expressed confidence that Golden State fans would tune in from wherever they had to despite the 9:30 a.m. tipoff in California.

Dream players including Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada and Angel Reese brushed aside the game time as a nonfactor.

"It's the Finals," Gray said. "We just got to do what we've got to do. We are locked in on winning Game 6 whether it's 8 a.m., 10 p.m., midnight. We got a championship to win."

Evloev, who lost for the first time in his career, and Dvalishvili, an ex-champ who dropped his second straight to Yan, maintain their No. 2 rankings.

Other fights on the Abu Dhabi card did affect rankings. Light heavyweight Dominick Reyes was the lone fighter to defeat someone ranked higher than him, knocking out sixth-ranked light heavyweight Azamat Murzakanov. Reyes moves from No. 7 to the top five, and Murzakanov falls to Reyes' former spot.

Heavyweight saw a trickle-down succession of movement, partly due to a fight result. Alexander Volkov, who beat unranked Rizvan Kuniev, moves up one position to No. 3, largely because former UFC champion Tom Aspinall, previously ranked second, has been removed from the top 10 as ineligible because he has not fought in over a year. The other ranked heavyweights each move up one spot, and Kuniev enters the rankings at No. 10.

The other ranking change is at men's flyweight, where Lone'er Kavanagh climbs one position to No. 6 after handing unranked Ramazan Temirov his first loss.
